newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Official warns HK against subversion.
newsitem.headline: Official warns HK against subversion.

text.p: Hong Kong's Chief Secretary Anson Chan warned in remarks released on Friday that China would crack down on the territory if it became a base for subversion after Beijing resumes control.
We put our own autonomy at risk if we lead China's leaders to believe we are trying to undermine their system," Chan wrote in an article in a new book, Hello Goodbye, by journalist Michael Chugani.

"You can be sure China will clamp down hard if it suspects we are allowing Hong Kong to be used as a base for subversive activities. Chinese action of this sort would be disastrous for Hong Kong," she said.
Hong Kong, a British colony for 156 years, reverts to Beijing control at midnight on June 30.
China has pledged to let the territory of 6.4 million keep its economic and political way of life unchanged for 50 years.
Chan also said the best way to protect Hong Kong's autonomy after the July 1 handover was to stay out of China's domestic affairs.
"Minding our own business is the best guarantee of our autonomy. We cannot expect China to keep its nose out of our system if we stick our noses into theirs," she said.
Chan, who is deputy to Governor Chris Patten, will retain her post as the head Hong Kong's 180,000-strong civil service after future leader Tung Chee-hwa takes over on July 1.
